summary: Marco Walther works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, attested in 2017, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard and also studied under Khenpo Dondrub Namgyal.

Marcus Bingenheimer specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Nagoya University and the University of Würzburg (PhD ~2000–2004 under Norbert Klaes). His positions include posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, and Temple University.

Marek Mejor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a Michael Coulson Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and served as a professor at the University of Warsaw, attested between 2000 and 2010.

Marek Zemánek specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at Seoul National University, Dongguk University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under the supervision of Radek Chlup.

Margaret Dornish is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California. Attested in 1989, she served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College.
Margaret Gouin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret Mead (1901–1978) studied at DePauw University, Barnard College, and Columbia University. She held long-term posts at the American Museum of Natural History (~1926–1978) and Columbia University (~1954–1978), as well as the University of Rhode Island (~1969–1971).

Margaret R. Miles (b. 1937) works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at San Francisco State University and the Graduate Theological Union. She held posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and Harvard University (attested 1999).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Attested in 2016, she completed her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower; she also studied under postdoctoral mentor Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya (1933–2021) was an Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar educated at St. Petersburg University. She held long-term research positions at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts and Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2014), and visited Soka University and IRIAB.
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Karin Preisendanz and completed an MA under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes, attested in 2010.

Maria Heim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. After earning a BA at Reed College and a PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, she became Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Marianne Winder (1918–2001) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having studied at the University of London and SOAS. She worked at the University of Nottingham (~1953–1963) and was Keeper of the Oriental Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (~1964–1983).
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She completed her studies at the University of Pennsylvania, where she studied under Sengaku Maeda.

Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD in 2006 from Columbia University, where she studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, and John Stratton Hawley.

Mario D'Amato specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths and held positions at Hampshire College (attested 2001) and Rollins College in the Department of Philosophy and Religion.
Mario Kozah works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Cambridge under James Montgomery and held a post at the American University of Beirut.

Mario Poceski specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, earning his PhD in 2000 from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He has taught at the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019) and held visiting roles at Iowa and Stanford.
Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Matics studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

Mark A. Nathan specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD in 2010 at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Attested in 2010, he held posts at UCLA, Kangwon National University, and the University at Buffalo.
